Pursuant to Article 34 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek to institute a complaint against the perpetrator(s) for the alleged commission of the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property' under Article 265 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 265(1)(b) read with Article 265(2).

Under Article 23 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I request the registering of a First Information Report (FIR) and an investigation be initiated under Article 26(1) of the same Act.

Pursuant to Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek to adduce evidence of the occurrence, including the fact that the mobile phone was in my possession prior to its alleged theft and that it was stolen during the commotion in the crowded bus.

## Summary
Based on the given context, you are seeking to institute a complaint against the perpetrator(s) for the alleged commission of the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property' under Article 265 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 265(1)(b) read with Article 265(2). Your mobile phone was stolen from your pocket in a crowded bus.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 314]

## Recommendation / next steps
Given that the perpetrator(s) stole your mobile phone, which is a movable property, and considering the context of [BNS Section 314], it is likely that the perpetrator(s) have committed the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property'. I recommend that you file a complaint with the authorities, providing details of the incident, including the time, place, and circumstances of the theft. The authorities will then register a First Information Report (FIR) under Article 26(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 and initiate an investigation. As evidence, you can adduce details of your possession of the mobile phone prior to its theft and the fact that it was stolen during the commotion in the crowded bus, which can be considered under Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Accordingly, a Bill, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 was introduced in the Lok Sabha 
on 11th August, 2023. The Bill was referred to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs for its consideration and report. The Committee after deliberations made its 
recommendations in its report submitted on 10th November, 2023. The recommendations made by the 
Committee have been considered by the Government and it has been decided to withdraw the Bill 
pending in Lok Sabha and introduce a new Bill incorporating therein those recommendations made by the 
Committee that have been accepted by the Government.

Petition for Investigation and Prosecution Pursuant to Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

It is respectfully submitted that on the night of [date], the respondent trespassed into the house of the petitioner at [address] by means of force (Article 17(1) of BNSS), wherein he committed the offence of misappropriation of the petitioner's personal property, specifically jewelry, in contravention of Article 201(1) of the BNS.

The petitioner humbly requests that an investigation be conducted under Article 123(2) of the BNS to identify the respondent and secure evidence of the said offence, and that the respondent be prosecuted in accordance with Article 17(1) of the BNSS and Article 201(1) of the BNS.

Supporting documents and evidence are attached hereto.

Please accept this petition as a formal complaint.

Respectfully submitted,
[Petitioner's Name]
result.answer:
## Summary
The petitioner, a house owner, has been victimized by a trespasser who broke into their house at night and stole their jewelry. The petitioner has filed a petition for investigation and prosecution under Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 201] 
[BNS Section 4] 
[BNS Section 209] 
[BNS Section 199] 

## Recommendation / next steps
The Magistrate is respectfully requested to order an investigation under Article 123(2) of the BNS to identify the respondent and secure evidence of the said offence. The respondent should be prosecuted in accordance with Article 17(1) of the BNSS and Article 201(1) of the BNS.

Additionally, the Magistrate may consider Section 199 of the BNS, which deals with public servants disobeying direction under law, in case the investigation reveals any discrepancies or omissions on the part of the public servants involved.

Further, in accordance with Section 209 of the BNS, the Magistrate may consider imposing community service as a punishment for the respondent, depending on the severity of the offence and the circumstances of the case.

Finally, the Magistrate is requested to ensure that the investigation and prosecution are conducted in a fair and impartial manner, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and the provisions of the BNS.

Your neighbor's statements threatening to cause bodily harm to you if you use the common parking area may constitute an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). In view of the potential for your neighbor's statements to constitute an offence under BNS, you may want to consider reporting these incidents to the authorities or seeking a restraining order to prevent further harassment. result.answer:
## Summary

The recipient of the abusive and vulgar messages has committed an offence under Article 12 of BNS, specifically Section 12(1)(a) - 'Malignant Communication', by sending repeated messages with intent to harm or harass the complainant. This may be classified as a 'continuing offence' under Article 12(2) of BNS. To lodge a complaint and obtain necessary protection orders, the complainant can follow the procedure under Chapter VII - 'Protective Orders for Victims of Harassment and Malignant Communication' of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). Admissibility of WhatsApp messages as evidence under Article 21 - 'Digital Communication Evidence' of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) is possible, and the messages will be considered relevant and reliable evidence in a court of law.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 12]
- [BNS Section 356] (defamation, exceptions)
- [BNS Section 353] (Statements conducing to public mischief)
- [BNS Section 232] (Threatening any person to give false evidence)
- [BNS Section 78] (Stalking)
- [BNS Section 209] (Non-appearance in response to a proclamation)
- [BNS Section 75] (Sexual harassment)
- [BNS Section 4] (proposed new law and offences)

## Recommendation / next steps

1. The complainant should lodge a complaint with the police or the relevant authorities under Chapter VII - 'Protective Orders for Victims of Harassment and Malignant Communication' of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).
2. The complainant should provide evidence of the abusive and vulgar messages, including screenshots or printouts of the messages, to support the complaint.
3. The complainant should also provide any other relevant evidence, such as witness statements or other documentation, to support the complaint.
4. The police or authorities will investigate the complaint and may issue a protection order or take other action as necessary.
5. In court, the WhatsApp messages will be considered relevant and reliable evidence, and the defendant may be held liable for the offence of 'Malignant Communication' under Article 12 of BNS.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished

Query:

Pursuant to Article 34, Clause 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), has the landlord committed the offence of wrongful confinement or illegal detention under Article 42, Section 1 of BNS, by locking out the tenant from the rented premises without lawful notice, thereby rendering the tenant unable to access their personal belongings as mentioned under Article 19, Section 5 of BNS? 

Additionally, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what procedures can be initiated under Chapter 3, Article 7, to secure the release of the tenant's belongings and ensure the landlord's compliance with the relevant laws?
result.answer:
## Summary

The landlord has locked the tenant out of the rented room without any notice, rendering the tenant unable to access their personal belongings. This situation raises concerns about wrongful confinement and the tenant's rights under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 127] - Wrongful confinement
- [BNS Section 211] - Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the given scenario, it appears that the landlord's actions may constitute wrongful confinement under [BNS Section 127]. This is because the landlord has restrained the tenant in such a manner that prevents them from proceeding beyond certain circumscribing limits, i.e., the tenant is locked out of their room.

The tenant may be eligible for compensation for non-treatment under [BNS Section 200] if the landlord fails to provide access to their belongings. However, the tenant may need to take further action to secure their release, which could involve initiating procedures under Chapter 3, Article 7 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to secure the release of their belongings and ensure the landlord's compliance with the relevant laws.

Pursuant to Article 43 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal complaint for consideration:

Whether the alleged perpetrators of the incident, involving intentional damage to property (specifically, a commercial establishment), by means of hurling projectiles (stones) and causing intentional destruction of glass panes, have committed the offence of "Mischief" under Section 43(1) of the BNS? 

Additionally, I request an investigation into the circumstances surrounding this incident, as mandated by Section 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), with a view to determining whether the perpetrators were acting in contravention of Sections 13 and 14 of the BNSS, which pertain to the maintenance of public order and the prevention of unlawful assemblies.

Furthermore, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the identification of the perpetrators and the reconstruction of the events surrounding the incident, in light of Article 17(2) of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of circumstantial evidence.

## Summary

Based on the provided context, it appears that the group of people damaged your shop during a protest by throwing stones and breaking the glass. You have filed a formal complaint under Article 43 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), seeking to determine whether the perpetrators committed the offence of "Mischief" under Section 43(1) of the BNS.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 324] - deals with the offence of mischief, which may be applicable to the damage caused to the shop.

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the facts of the case, it seems that the perpetrators may have committed the offence of mischief under Section 324 of the BNS. Therefore, it is recommended that the case be investigated further to determine the extent of the damage and the identities of the perpetrators.

Section 324 of the BNS provides for punishment for mischief, which may extend to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both, depending on the extent of the damage caused.

Additionally, since the incident occurred during a protest, it may be relevant to investigate whether the perpetrators were acting in contravention of Sections 13 and 14 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), which pertain to the maintenance of public order and the prevention of unlawful assemblies.

It would be best to consult with the relevant authorities and experts to determine the next steps and to ensure that the investigation is conducted in accordance with the provisions of the BNS and the BNSS.

Application of Section 306 of BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023) for alleged offences under Section 506 of BNS, seeking redress under Section 155 of BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) for protection and investigation.

Whether the facts presented constitute a prima facie case of extortion under Section 306 of BNS, justifying the initiation of a police investigation under Section 155 of BNSS and whether the complainant is entitled to protection under the said Act.

Further, this application seeks clarification on the admissibility of electronic evidence, including voice messages and SMS, as per Article 59 of BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) for purposes of prosecution under Section 306 of BNS.
result.answer:
## Summary

The facts presented indicate that a stranger is threatening to burn the complainant's shop unless they pay money. This behavior constitutes a prima facie case of extortion under Section 308 of BNS, as the stranger is intentionally putting the complainant in fear of injury to their shop and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver money. The complainant is entitled to protection under Section 155 of BNSS for protection and investigation.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Section 308 (Extortion)
- Section 155 of BNSS (Protection and investigation)
- [BNS Section 5]

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the prima facie case of extortion, the complainant should file a complaint under Section 155 of BNSS for protection and investigation. The police should be informed about the electronic evidence, including voice messages and SMS, which can be used as admissible evidence under Article 59 of BSA. The complainant should also be advised to preserve any relevant evidence and to cooperate fully with the investigation.

Petition for Relief under Article 39(1)(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS): 

Complainant seeks immediate action against the perpetrator who, with malicious intent, committed an act of cybercrime by hacking into the complainant's social media account and posting content deemed offensive under Article 11(6) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). Prayer is made for the registration of an FIR as per Article 23(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and for necessary investigation under Article 46(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Further, this petition seeks the exclusion of the offending content as evidence under Article 56(2) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) and any other relief deemed fit and necessary by the court to protect the complainant's reputation and ensure the perpetrator's accountability for their actions.

## Summary
The complainant has been a victim of cybercrime, where their social media account was hacked and used to post offensive content under Article 11(6) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). The complainant seeks relief under Article 39(1)(b) of BNS, including the registration of an FIR under Article 23(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), investigation under Article 46(1) of BNSS, exclusion of the offending content as evidence under Article 56(2) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), and other necessary relief to protect their reputation and ensure accountability.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 353] (Statements conducing to public mischief)
[BNS Section 197] (Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration)
[BNS Section 211] (Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it)
[BNS Section 113] (Terrorist act)

## Recommendation / next steps
Given the nature of the offense, the most relevant provision appears to be Section 353, which deals with statements conducing to public mischief. This section could be applied to the situation, as the posting of offensive content on the complainant's social media account could be seen as making a false statement or report with the intent to cause fear or alarm to the public.

However, to ensure the complainant receives the desired relief, it is recommended that the court investigate the circumstances surrounding the hacking of the social media account and the posting of the offensive content. This may involve gathering evidence and interviewing witnesses.

Additionally, the court may need to consider other provisions, such as Section 197, which deals with imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration, if the offending content is found to have caused disharmony or feelings of enmity between different groups.

In any case, the court should expedite the matter and ensure fair and just treatment of the complainant, as requested under Article 5(2) of BNS.

In the event of a homicide committed during a dispute over immovable property, the circumstances of the incident where your uncle allegedly stabbed your father multiple times with a sharp-edged object, resulting in his instantaneous demise, would attract charges under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 4]
- [BNS Section 230]
- [BNS Section 113]
- [BNS Section 303]

## Recommendation / next steps

To register a First Information Report (FIR) and commence an investigation in this case, you should approach the nearest police station and provide them with the details of the incident. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the police should register an FIR and initiate an investigation into the matter.

To establish the guilt of the accused, the admissible evidence that can be used under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) includes the testimony of witnesses, any physical evidence collected from the crime scene, and any other relevant facts and circumstances of the case. The relevant provisions of the BNS, specifically [BNS Section 230] and [BNS Section 113], may be applicable in this case.

It is essential to note that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) has replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), and all relevant provisions and sections should be referred to accordingly.

Complaint against Unauthorised Use of Personal Information and Defamation under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 123 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek your assistance in filing a complaint against an individual who has committed the offence of unauthorised use of personal information under Article 234(1)(a) of BNS, whereby my social media account was accessed without my consent, and offensive content was posted using my name.

Furthermore, under Article 219 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I also seek to file a complaint against the said individual for the offence of defamation, as the said content has caused harm to my reputation and goodwill.

Under Section 53(4) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that the investigation be conducted expeditiously, and the accused be brought to justice.

Pursuant to Article 17 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I submit the following documents as evidence:

* Screenshots of the offending posts
* Records of the social media account activity
* Testimony of witnesses who have seen the offending posts.

I request that the authorities take immediate action in this matter, investigate the circumstances surrounding the unauthorised use of my personal information and the posting of defamatory content, and bring the accused to justice in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

## Summary
You have had your social media account hacked and offensive content posted using your name. You would like to file a complaint against the individual who committed this act under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for unauthorized use of personal information and defamation.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 1]
[BNS Section 234]
[BNS Section 219]
[BNS Section 197]
[BNS Section 353]
[BNS Section 356]

## Recommendation / next steps
You should file a complaint with the authorities, providing the required documents as evidence, including screenshots of the offending posts, records of the social media account activity, and testimony of witnesses who have seen the offending posts. The authorities should conduct an expeditious investigation and bring the accused to justice in accordance with the provisions of BNS. You may also want to consider seeking legal advice to ensure that your complaint is properly prepared and presented.

## Summary
The complainant seeks to file a formal complaint under Section 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the alleged commission of the offence of Murder. Additionally, an order is sought to conduct an inquest into the cause of death of the deceased under Article 176 of the BNSS. It is also requested to direct the collection of evidence, including forensic reports, to determine the extent of the injuries caused to the deceased and to establish the culpability of the accused.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 302], [BNS Section 176], [BNS Section 65], [BNS Section 317]

## Recommendation / next steps
The court may consider the complaint filed under Section 302 of BNS and may direct the police to conduct an inquest into the cause of death of the deceased under Article 176 of BNSS. The court may also direct the collection of evidence, including forensic reports, to determine the extent of the injuries caused to the deceased and to establish the culpability of the accused. The accused may be charged under Section 317 of BNS for the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt by means of poison, corrosive substance or hot substance, as the accused allegedly poured acid on the victim's face.

The accused's actions, if proven, may lead to severe penalties, including imprisonment for life and fine under Article 302 and Article 315 of the BNS. The accused may also be charged with false evidence if they intentionally provide false information or evidence during the investigation or trial.

## Summary

A complaint has been filed against a neighbor who allegedly hit the complainant's brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument, leaving the brother in ICU and possibly facing life-threatening injuries. The complaint alleges offenses of "Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder" (Section 306, BNS) and "Murder" (Section 307, BNS). An application has been made to register an FIR under Section 154, BNSS. The admissibility of evidence, including statements made by the injured party and medical evidence, is also being questioned.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 299]
- [BNS Section 302]
- [BNS Section 306]
- [BNS Section 307]
- [Section 154, BNSS]
- [BNS Section 59]
- [BNS Section 60]

## Recommendation / next steps

It appears that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) is the applicable law in this case. To proceed, the police should register an FIR under Section 154, BNSS and investigate the incident. The admissibility of evidence, including statements made by the injured party and medical evidence, should be determined in accordance with [BNS Section 59] and [BNS Section 60]. The complainant's brother's statement, if made before hospitalization, may be admissible under [BNS Section 59]. Medical evidence, including hospital records, may also be admissible under [BNS Section 60]. The investigation should focus on gathering evidence to establish the facts of the case and determine whether the alleged offenses of "Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder" and "Murder" have been committed. The complainant should be consulted throughout the investigation to ensure that their rights are protected.

To the Hon'ble Magistrate of the District Court,

Pursuant to the alleged incident of a female individual being found hanging in her room within a span of two years of her marriage, there is a reasonable suspicion of her having been subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws for dowry. It is requested that an investigation be conducted under Article 21 of the Constitution of India and Section 176 of the BNSS to determine the circumstances surrounding the deceased's death.

It is respectfully prayed that:

result.rephrased_query: Whether the convict, having been released on parole under the provisions of Section 53 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and having committed the alleged offences of Section 302 read with Section 304 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, is liable for prosecution and what would be the appropriate course of action to be taken by the authorities in terms of Section 12 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 and Section 22 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 in gathering and admissibility of evidence in this case.
result.answer:
## Summary
A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death. The convict is liable for prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 for the alleged offences of Section 302 and Section 304.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 302] (murder)
- [BNS Section 304] (punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder)
- [BNS Section 12] (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – powers of a magistrate)
- [BNS Section 22] (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 – gathering and admissibility of evidence)

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, the convict is liable for prosecution for the alleged offences of murder and culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The authorities should proceed with the investigation and gather evidence according to the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The magistrate, as per the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall have the power to investigate and take necessary actions in this case. The convict's parole should be revoked, and he should be taken into custody to face trial for the alleged offences.

Subject: Query regarding alleged commission of offence under BNS, 2023 - Suicidal Death of Spouse

Respected Hon'ble Magistrate/Judge,

I seek your esteemed guidance on the following matter:

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 302 of the BNS, 2023, I would like to inquire about the applicability of the offence of Dowry Harassment as defined under Article 498 (2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023, in the following scenario:

A married woman (hereinafter referred to as the "deceased") was subjected to continuous harassment and torture by her husband and his family members (hereinafter referred to as the "accused") for dowry within a period of two years from the date of marriage. The deceased was found deceased, allegedly by hanging, in her room on a certain date.

In light of the aforesaid circumstances, I kindly request Your Honour to clarify whether the accused can be held liable under Article 498 (2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023, for the alleged commission of the offence.

Additionally, I would like to seek Your Honour's guidance on the procedure to be followed under the BNSS, 2023, for registering an FIR (First Information Report) and conducting an investigation into this matter.

Furthermore, I would appreciate Your Honour's clarification on the admissibility of evidence under the BSA, 2023, and the burden of proof that would lie on the prosecution in establishing the guilt of the accused.

I look forward to receiving Your Honour's guidance and assistance in this matter.

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]

The accused can be held liable under Section 80 of the BNS, 2023, specifically for the offence of dowry death. The husband and in-laws can be held liable under the provisions of the BNS, 2023, for the alleged commission of the offence, and the court will have to determine the appropriate punishment based on the evidence presented.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

[BNS Section 4] BNS_2023_s4 (Act: BNS_2023)
Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Pursuant to Article 123(2)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek guidance on the following matter:

Can a person be held liable for an attempt to cause grievous hurt under Section 316 of BNS, where an indivividual intentionally discharges a firearm, licensed or otherwise, in a situation of provocation and dispute, resulting in a narrowly missed shot directed at another person, with whom they share a business partnership?

Please note that the circumstances surrounding the incident may be relevant to determining the applicability of relevant provisions and the quantum of liability.
result.answer:
## Summary
The man fired a licensed gun at his business partner during a heated dispute, but the bullet missed narrowly. The question is whether he can be held liable for an attempt to cause grievous hurt under Section 316 of BNS, given the circumstances of the incident.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 53]
- [BNS Section 122]
- [BNS Section 118]
- [BNS Section 51]
- [BNS Section 25]

## Recommendation / next steps
Under [BNS Section 53], the man could be held liable for the effect caused by his actions, even if it was different from what he intended. Since he fired a licensed gun, he might be able to claim that he did not intend to cause grievous hurt, but under [BNS Section 25], if he knew that his actions were likely to cause harm, he could still be held liable.

However, given the circumstances of the incident, [BNS Section 122] might be more applicable. If the man was provoked by his business partner and did not intend to cause grievous hurt, he might only be liable for a lesser punishment. 

Further investigation and evidence would be needed to determine the man's intent and the actual harm caused. Therefore, the court should consider [BNS Section 118] and other relevant provisions to determine the appropriate punishment and liability for the man's actions.

Pursuant to Section 176(1)(g) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a complaint is made against the husband and in-laws of the deceased for alleged commission of the offence under Section 312(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), read with Sections 312(2) and 312(3) thereof, arising out of the continuous harassment and torture inflicted upon the deceased by the accused.

The circumstances of the case, including the fact that the deceased was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage, necessitate an investigation to ascertain whether the death was caused by the accused's acts constituting the aforesaid offence.

The prosecution is required to prove the guilt of the accused under Section 101(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), which provides that the burden of proving the defence of the accused lies on them. Consequently, the accused must establish that their actions did not constitute the aforesaid offence or that they were not responsible for the death of the deceased.

The court is required to inquire into the circumstances surrounding the death and to determine whether the accused are guilty of the offence alleged against them, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and the provisions of the BNSS and the BNS.

Petition for Investigation and Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Honourable Magistrate,

Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I submit this petition for investigation and prosecution of the following offence:

The petitioner's daughter, a minor, allegedly posted a message on social media encouraging her classmate to take her own life, which ultimately led to the classmate's demise. This act may be considered an abetment to suicide under Article 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), as it appears to have instigated the classmate to take her own life.

Please consider initiating a magisterial inquiry under Section 19(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to investigate the said incident and determine the culpability of the petitioner's daughter. Furthermore, if found guilty, the petitioner seeks prosecution under Article 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for abetment to suicide.

The petitioner requests the Honourable Magistrate to expedite the inquiry and prosecution process under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]

## Summary

The petitioner's daughter, a minor, allegedly posted a message on social media encouraging her classmate to take her own life, which ultimately led to the classmate's demise. The petitioner seeks investigation and prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 305]

## Recommendation / next steps

The Honourable Magistrate is recommended to initiate a magisterial inquiry under Section 19(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to investigate the said incident and determine the culpability of the petitioner's daughter. If found guilty, the Honourable Magistrate may proceed with prosecution under [BNS Section 305] for abetment to suicide.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Committee on Home Affairs for its consideration and report. The Committee after deliberations made its 
recommendations in its report submitted on 10th November, 2023. The recommendations made by the 
Committee have been considered by the Government and it has been decided to withdraw the Bill 
pending in Lok Sabha and introduce a new Bill incorporating therein those recommendations made by the 
Committee that have been accepted by the Government.

Petition for Inquiry into Alleged Offence under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

Under Article 321, BNS, a complaint has been filed alleging that a person, in a state of rage and during a heated dispute, discharged a firearm, albeit licensed, resulting in a narrowly missed shot at another individual. 

The complainant seeks an investigation under Section 53 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to determine whether the alleged actions of the accused constitute an offence under Article 123, BNS, specifically regarding the use of a deadly weapon in a manner that endangers human life.

The complainant requests that any relevant evidence be collected and examined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly Article 27, which pertains to the admissibility of evidence in cases involving the use of physical force or weapons.

Further, the complainant seeks an assessment of the potential culpability of the accused under Article 145, BNS, which pertains to the culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

The complainant seeks an investigation to determine whether the accused's actions constitute an offence under Article 123, BNS, specifically regarding the use of a deadly weapon in a manner that endangers human life.

[BNS Section 1] 
[BNS Section 5]

The accused's potential culpability under Article 145, BNS, should also be assessed.

A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death. The query is whether this act constitutes an offence under Section 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and if it amounts to 'murder' thereby attracting the prescribed punishment. Additionally, the necessary steps to be taken by the authorities under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically in relation to Article 167 (arrest) and Article 168 (custody), considering the life-convict's status of being on parole at the time of the incident.

[BNS Section 1], [BNS Section 109]

The life-convict's act of strangling another person to death would amount to an attempt to murder under the provisions of Section 109 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. As the convict is on parole, the authorities must take immediate action under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. Pursuant to Article 168 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the convict must be taken into custody and produced before a magistrate as soon as possible.

The authorities must also take into account the provisions of Article 167 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, which deals with the arrest of a person. In this case, the life-convict's status as a parolee may require a different approach to arrest and custody, taking into account the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Further action would depend on the specific circumstances of the case and the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Whether the act of the cook, in mixing rat poison into the food served at the party, constitutes an offence under Article 304 of BNS, specifically with regard to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and whether such act may be classified as an 'offence of culpable homicide' (Article 304) given that three guests died as a result of consuming the poisoned food?

Pursuant to BNSS, what are the procedures to be followed by the investigating officer in collecting and preserving evidence related to this incident, particularly with respect to Articles 23-25 of BNSS, relating to the collection, preservation, and disposal of evidence?

## Summary

The cook mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and three guests died as a result. The question arises whether this act constitutes an offence under Article 304 of BNS, specifically with regard to culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Additionally, the procedures to be followed by the investigating officer in collecting and preserving evidence related to this incident, and the admissibility of certain evidence in court are also to be determined.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 1]
* [BNS Section 46]
* [BNS Section 148]
* [BNS Section 209]
* [BNS Section 1] (Explanation)
* [BNS Section 4]
* [BNS Section 9]

## Recommendation / next steps

Considering the BNS provisions, the cook's act of mixing rat poison into the food can be considered as an act of culpable homicide, as three guests died as a result. This is in line with the explanation provided in [BNS Section 1] (Explanation), where it is stated that the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an omission, is an offence.

The investigating officer should follow the procedures outlined in Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), specifically Articles 23-25, relating to the collection, preservation, and disposal of evidence.

Regarding the admissibility of evidence, the testimony of the cook, or any other witness, would be admissible as evidence under Article 12 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA), considering the circumstances of the incident and the provisions of Article 15 of BSA, relating to the credibility of witnesses.

It is also worth noting that conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147 can be considered, as provided in [BNS Section 148], where it is stated that several persons may be guilty of different offences by means of a criminal act. In this case, the cook and possibly others may have conspired to commit the offence of culpable homicide.

result.answer:
## Summary
A young woman was lured with a fake job offer, trafficked to another state, and forced into prostitution. The question is whether a prima facie case exists against the perpetrator(s) for the offences of Human Trafficking and Kidnapping/Abduction and Forcible Exploitation, and if the trafficked woman's testimony, corroborated by mobile phone records, bank statements, and eyewitness accounts, is sufficient to establish the chain of events and the complicity of the accused.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 13] 
[BNS Section 25] 
[BNS Section 4]
[BNS Section 199]
[BNS Section 211]
[BNS Section 339]

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the given context, a prima facie case exists against the perpetrator(s) for the offences of Human Trafficking and Kidnapping/Abduction and Forcible Exploitation. The trafficked woman's testimony, corroborated by mobile phone records, bank statements, and eyewitness accounts, is sufficient to establish the chain of events and the complicity of the accused. The public servant's failure to record information given under section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, as mentioned in section 199, may be relevant in this case. Additionally, the omission to give notice or information to a public servant by a person legally bound to do so, as mentioned in section 211, may also be applicable. Furthermore, the possession of a forged document, as described in section 337 or 338, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine, may be relevant in this case.

Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the following legal query is framed:

Whether the acts of the gang in kidnap and maiming children to exploit them for organized begging would constitute the offence of 'Crime against Humanity and the vulnerable' under Article 123 of BNS, and if so, what would be the appropriate punishment under Article 134 of BNS.

Further, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), whether the police would be justified in invoking Section 16 of BNSS, which deals with the arrest of persons involved in organized crime, and whether the court may order the police to exercise its powers under Section 17 of BNSS to confiscate the assets and properties acquired by the gang through the commission of the said offence.

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), whether the burden of proof would shift from the prosecution under Article 43 of BSA, to prove that the gang was involved in organized crime and that the children were exploited for begging, and what would be the relevant evidence required to prove the said offences.
result.answer:
## Summary
The gang's acts of kidnapping and maiming children to exploit them for organized begging would constitute the offence of 'organised crime' under BNS_2023_s111, and also 'Crime against Humanity and the vulnerable' under Article 123 of BNS. The appropriate punishment under Article 134 of BNS for organised crime in a case where the offence has resulted in the death of any person would be death or imprisonment for life, and a fine which shall not be less than ten lakh rupees.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- Section 111
- Section 139
- Section 148

## Recommendation / next steps
The police would be justified in invoking BNSS 2023 to arrest the persons involved in organised crime. The court may order the police to exercise its powers to confiscate the assets and properties acquired by the gang through the commission of the said offence. The burden of proof would not shift from the prosecution under BSA 2023. However, the relevant evidence required to prove the said offences could include testimonies from the victims or their families, medical records of the maimed children, and any other evidence that establishes the involvement of the gang in organised crime and exploitation of children for begging.

Pursuant to Article 302(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is alleged that the accused committed an act of attempted murder under Chapter V, Section 301(B) of the BNS, by discharging a firearm at his business partner, thereby endangering his life, albeit narrowly missing the target.

**Further Inquiries:**

1. **Article 13(2) of the BNSS:** Did the accused obtain valid permission to carry the firearm, as per the Arms Act, and whether such permit was valid at the time of the incident?
2. **Article 20(1) of the BNSS:** Was the accused aware that his actions may lead to harm to another person, particularly his business partner, during the heated dispute?
3. **Section 5(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA):** Is there any direct evidence, such as eyewitness accounts, video footage, or physical evidence, to establish the sequence of events leading to the alleged crime?
4. **Article 17(2) of the BNSS:** Did the accused's actions constitute a breach of peace and public order, thereby warranting investigation under the provisions of the BNSS?

Petition for Exhumation of Unlawful Custody and Protection of Juvenile.

To the Honorable Court,

I, the concerned parent, hereby invoke the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to seek the following relief:

Whether the action of a man, who met my minor daughter online, and subsequently took her away without my knowledge and consent, constitutes an offense under Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and if so, what measures can be taken to ensure the safe recovery of my daughter and the perpetrator's accountability?

Further, I request the Court to consider the provisions of Chapter VI of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the protection and recovery of my minor daughter, and to direct the concerned authorities to take necessary steps to prevent any tampering with evidence or obstruction of justice, as per Article 205 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Additionally, I seek the Court's guidance on the admissibility of digital evidence, as per the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), to establish the facts of the case and to identify the perpetrator.

I humbly request the Court to take immediate cognizance of this matter and to pass necessary orders to ensure the safety and well-being of my minor daughter, and to hold the perpetrator accountable for their actions.

Jai Hind.
result.answer:
## Summary
The concerned parent has petitioned the court for the recovery of their minor daughter who was taken away by a man she met online without the parent's knowledge or consent. The parent is seeking protection for the daughter and holding the perpetrator accountable.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 139] Kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging - This section could be relevant as it deals with kidnapping a child, which is the action taken by the man in this case.

## Recommendation / next steps
The court should take immediate cognizance of this matter and direct the concerned authorities to take necessary steps to recover the minor daughter and hold the perpetrator accountable. The court should also consider the provisions of Chapter VI of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for the protection and recovery of the minor daughter.

result.answer:
## Summary
The factory owner brought migrant workers from Bihar with false promises and made them work without pay under locked conditions. The question is whether this constitutes an offence under Article 123(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023), specifically the offence of "Deprivation of Labour Rights" punishable under Article 123(2)(d) thereof.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 111] (Dealing with Organised Crime), [BNS Section 148] (Conspiracy to commit offences), [BNS Section 324] (Mischief), [BNS Section 193] (Liability of owner, occupier, etc., of land on which an unlawful assembly or riot takes place), [BNS Section 200] (Punishment for non-treatment of victim) (Note: This section is not directly related to the query, but the concept of punishment for non-treatment of victim might be relevant)

## Recommendation / next steps
The actions of the factory owner could potentially be classified under various sections of the BNS_2023, including organised crime, conspiracy, mischief, and liability of owner/occupier. To determine the exact offence and punishment, a thorough investigation and analysis of the facts would be necessary. The documentary evidence, as per Article 56(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, would also be crucial in substantiating the prosecution initiated under Chapter VII of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. It is recommended that a detailed examination of the relevant BNS_2023 provisions be conducted to determine the most applicable sections and corresponding punishments.

Pursuant to Article 321 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is submitted to investigate the alleged commission of an offence under Section 366A of BNS, specifically the offence of "Abduction of a woman with intent to compel her for marriage" and/or Section 354 of BNS, which may include the offence of "Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty". Furthermore, we seek an inquiry into the possibility of the commission of an offence under Section 342 of BNS, "Wrongful confinement", as it pertains to the unlawful restriction of the woman's liberty, in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). 

In light of the above, please direct the investigation to be conducted in accordance with the procedures delineated in the BNSS, particularly Article 15 thereof, and provide evidence in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 11, concerning the admissibility of oral evidence.

## Summary
A woman passenger was forcibly taken by an auto-rickshaw driver to an isolated area against her will. This incident has been reported under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023) for alleged commission of offences under Section 366A (Abduction of a woman with intent to compel her for marriage), Section 354 (Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty), and Section 342 (Wrongful confinement).

## Applicable BNS provisions
- Section 366A
- Section 354
- Section 342
- Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for procedures of investigation)
- Article 11 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (for admissibility of oral evidence)

## Recommendation / next steps
The investigation should be conducted as per the procedures outlined in Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. The admissibility of oral evidence should be considered as per Article 11 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The complainant should provide all necessary information and evidence to support the alleged offences. The investigation should focus on gathering evidence and corroborating witness statements to determine the guilt or innocence of the accused.

Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, what would be the penal consequences under Section 304A for the cook who, with the intention of causing harm, mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and caused the death of three guests?

Furthermore, under Article 22(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, would the cook be considered a "culpable homicide not amounting to murder" under Section 299, and if so, what would be the relevant provisions of Article 14(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 that would govern the investigation and prosecution of this case?

Additionally, under Article 15(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what would be the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly with regards to the testimony of the cook and any other witnesses who may have observed the cook mixing the rat poison into the food, in light of Article 25(2) and Article 27(1) of the said Act?
result.answer:
## Summary
The cook intentionally mixed rat poison into the food served at a party, causing the death of three guests. This act is considered a criminal offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 304A]
[BNS Section 299]
[BNS Section 109]
[BNS Section 46]
[BNS Section 111]
[BNS Section 324]

## Recommendation / next steps
Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the BNS_2023, the cook can be punished under Section 304A for causing death by a negligent act. The cook's intention to cause harm and the subsequent death of three guests would be considered a culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 299.

Under Article 22(3) of the BNS_2023, the cook would be considered a culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The relevant provisions of Article 14(2) of the Bharati Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 would govern the investigation and prosecution of this case.

Under Article 15(1) of the Bharati Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the admissibility of evidence in this case would depend on the specific circumstances. The testimony of the cook and any other witnesses who may have observed the cook mixing the rat poison into the food would be admissible under Article 25(2) and Article 27(1) of the said Act.

The penalties for the cook would depend on the specific circumstances and the provisions of the BNS_2023. However, under Section 111, the cook could be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than five lakh rupees.

result.rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 34(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the accused persons can be held liable for the offences of 'Trafficking in Persons for Commercial Sexual Exploitation' under Article 12(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and if so, whether the victims can claim any relief under Article 44(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and whether the prosecution can proceed under Section 16 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for the collection and preservation of evidence, including medical reports and testimonials from the victims, in accordance with provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, particularly under Articles 15-18 thereof, in this case where the victims' testimonies are crucial for establishing the offence?
result.answer:
## Summary
The question pertains to whether the accused persons can be held liable for 'Trafficking in Persons for Commercial Sexual Exploitation' under Article 12(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and if so, whether the victims can claim any relief under Article 44(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

## Applicable BNS provisions

## Recommendation / next steps
To answer the given query, we must consider the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023). The BNS_2023 repeals the Indian Penal Code and introduces new provisions for offences and penalties.

 Article 12(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 pertains to 'Trafficking in Persons for Commercial Sexual Exploitation'. According to [BNS Section 111], whoever commits the offence of organised crime shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than five lakh rupees.

Considering the context, the accused persons can be held liable for 'Trafficking in Persons for Commercial Sexual Exploitation' under Article 12(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

As for the victims claiming relief under Article 44(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, it is not clear from the given context what specific provision Article 44(2) pertains to.

The prosecution can proceed under Section 16 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for the collection and preservation of evidence, including medical reports and testimonials from the victims, in accordance with provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

It is recommended that further investigation and legal proceedings be initiated against the accused persons under Article 12(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The victims may also be eligible for relief under Article 44(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, subject to the specific provisions of this article.

Whether the transaction between the couple and the orphanage caretaker, where the couple purchased a 4-year-old boy without the lawful authority of the caretaker, constitutes an offence under Article 22 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically with regard to the elements of "unlawful compulsory separation" and "abduction from lawful custody" under the aforesaid provision.

Further, whether the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) provides for the necessary measures of protection and safeguarding of the child's rights, and whether the police are under a statutory obligation to investigate and take appropriate action under Article 96 of the BNSS, considering the orphanage caretaker's actions as a potential case of illegal dealing in human beings or child trafficking.

Furthermore, what are the admissibility and relevance of evidence regarding the transaction, including the records of the orphanage and the consent or otherwise of the biological parents, under Article 43 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), and whether such evidence may be used to establish the guilt or otherwise of the caretaker and the couple.
result.answer:
## Summary
The couple bought a 4-year-old boy from an orphanage caretaker who had no authority to sell children. This transaction raises concerns about the unlawful compulsory separation of the child and potential child trafficking.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 139] 
- [BNS Section 137]
- [BNS Section 4]

## Recommendation / next steps
Given the facts, the orphanage caretaker's actions may constitute kidnapping or abduction from lawful guardianship, as the caretaker did not have the lawful authority to sell the child. This is particularly concerning under [BNS Section 137], which defines kidnapping from lawful guardianship.

The police are under a statutory obligation to investigate and take appropriate action under Article 96 of the BNSS, considering the caretaker's actions as a potential case of illegal dealing in human beings or child trafficking.

To establish the guilt or otherwise of the caretaker and the couple, evidence regarding the transaction, including the records of the orphanage and the consent or otherwise of the biological parents, will be crucial. Under Article 43 of the BSA, the admissibility and relevance of such evidence need to be evaluated.

Given the seriousness of the offense, the caretaker and the couple may be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine under [BNS Section 139].

Pursuant to Article 121 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following complaint: 

On a date and time yet to be ascertained, three individuals, riding a motorcycle, committed the offence of 'Theft' (Article 47, BNS) by forcibly taking possession of my gold chain while I was lawfully on a public thoroughfare. 

Moreover, one of the perpetrators displayed a 'Deadly Weapon' (Article 34, BNS) in furtherance of the aforesaid crime, namely a knife. 

I request that necessary steps be taken under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to investigate this incident and apprehend the culprits.

In accordance with the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I am available to provide further evidence and assistance in the investigation of this case.
result.answer:
## Summary
The complainant was robbed of their gold chain by three men on a motorcycle. The complainant was walking on the road and the perpetrators used a knife to intimidate them. This incident falls under the category of 'Theft' as per Article 47, BNS. The perpetrators also displayed a 'Deadly Weapon' in furtherance of the crime, which is an aggravating factor.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 4]
- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 47]
- [BNS Section 34]
- [BNS Section 303]

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the perpetrator(s) of the crime can be charged under Section 47 for theft and Section 34 for displaying a deadly weapon in furtherance of the crime. The punishment for theft under Section 303 can range from imprisonment to a fine, depending on the circumstances of the case. The complainant should cooperate with the investigation and provide any additional evidence or assistance as required. The authorities should take necessary steps to apprehend the perpetrators and bring them to justice.

Whether the commission of an offence under Article 123(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (theft of gold and valuables from a commercial establishment by a group of more than five persons) and Article 123(1)(b) (theft of cash from a commercial establishment by a group of more than five persons) can be substantiated by the evidence of eyewitness testimony in the form of a complaint lodged by the watchman, who was present at the scene of the crime at the time of the incident, as per Article 78(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, and whether the watchman's statement can be admitted as a dying declaration under Article 32(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, despite the fact that the watchman is not a dying person, but was overpowered by the accused.

Whether a police officer, acting under Article 21(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, has the power to arrest and detain the accused in this case, and whether the detention is lawful under Article 21(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, requiring a magistrate's order under Article 22(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, or can the police officer exercise the power to arrest and detain the accused under Article 22(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, based on the availability of sufficient evidence under Article 21(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

## Summary

In this case, a gang of seven armed men broke into a jewellery shop at night, tied up the watchman, and looted all the gold and cash. The question is whether the commission of an offence under Article 123(1)(a) and Article 123(1)(b) can be substantiated by the evidence of eyewitness testimony in the form of a complaint lodged by the watchman. Additionally, whether the watchman's statement can be admitted as a dying declaration under Article 32(2), despite the fact that the watchman is not a dying person but was overpowered by the accused.

Furthermore, the question is whether a police officer, acting under Article 21(1), has the power to arrest and detain the accused in this case, and whether the detention is lawful under Article 21(2), requiring a magistrate's order under Article 22(1), or can the police officer exercise the power to arrest and detain the accused under Article 22(2), based on the availability of sufficient evidence under Article 21(3).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 111]
- [BNS Section 148]

## Recommendation / next steps

Considering that the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023) are applicable, the watchman's statement can be considered as a complaint under Article 123(1)(a) and Article 123(1)(b) for substantiating the commission of an offence by the gang of seven armed men. However, for the statement to be admitted as a dying declaration, the watchman must meet the criteria under Article 32(2), which requires that the person making the statement is dead or about to die and that the statement relates to the cause or circumstances of what is believed to be the person's death.

Regarding the police officer's power to arrest and detain the accused, under Article 21(1), the officer may arrest the accused if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the accused has committed an offence. However, under Article 21(2), the detention of the accused must be lawful and in accordance with the provisions of the BNS_2023. Article 22(1) requires a magistrate's order for the detention of an accused, but Article 22(2) provides an exception, allowing for the detention of an accused if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the accused will cause harm to themselves or others, or that the accused will flee the jurisdiction.

Therefore, in this case, the police officer may exercise the power to arrest and detain the accused under Article 22(2), based on the availability of sufficient evidence under Article 21(3).

repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed

Pursuant to Article 5 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek clarification on the following:

Is the alleged individual, who is reportedly extorting money under the threat of violence and inflicting physical harm on unwilling recipients, committing the offence of 'Extortion with the intention of causing physical harm' as defined in Article 14 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023?

Furthermore, under Article 2 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the procedures for reporting and lodging a complaint in connection with the said incident, particularly with regards to the protection of the complainant and witnesses?

Additionally, under Article 17 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what is the admissibility of the complainant's testimony in light of their alleged involvement in the transactions with the accused, and what are the relevant provisions for determining the credibility and reliability of their statement?
result.answer:
## Summary

The individual in question is reportedly extorting money from shopkeepers under the threat of violence, causing physical harm to those who refuse to pay. This description matches the offence of 'Extortion with the intention of causing physical harm' as defined in Section 308 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The extorter puts the shopkeepers in fear of injury and dishonestly induces them to deliver property or valuable security.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 308] 
- [BNS Section 209]

## Recommendation / next steps

To report the incident, the procedures under Article 2 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 should be followed. The complainant and witnesses should be protected to ensure their safety and cooperation during the investigation and trial. 

Regarding the admissibility of the complainant's testimony, Article 17 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 may provide relevant provisions for determining the credibility and reliability of their statement. However, since the question does not provide the relevant BNS context for Article 17, we cannot cite the exact section.

Pursuant to Article 12(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request to report an alleged commission of the offence of "Abduction of a Minor" and/or "Kidnapping" as defined in Article 18(2)(c) of BNS, in contravention of Article 19(3)(a) of BNSS, which mandates the reporting of missing persons.

Noting that the victim is a minor, I request an investigation into this incident under Article 20(1)(i) of BNSS, ensuring the preservation of evidence and the protection of the rights of the minor as an informant under Article 21(4)(b) of BNSS.

Further, I request an examination of the online interactions between the victim and the alleged perpetrator, in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with respect to the admissibility of digital evidence under Article 35(2)(d) of BSA, and the reliability of online testimony as per Article 42(1)(a) of BSA.

I request the authorities to take necessary measures to locate and secure the safe return of the minor, and to initiate proceedings against the alleged perpetrator as per Article 28(1)(c) of BNSS.

You have reported the incident and requested an investigation, ensuring the preservation of evidence and the protection of the rights of the minor as an informant. You also want the authorities to examine the online interactions between the victim and the alleged perpetrator and take necessary measures to locate and secure the safe return of the minor.

- [BNS Section 19(3)(a)]
- [BNS Section 20(1)(i)]
- [BNS Section 21(4)(b)]
- [BNS Section 35(2)(d)]
- [BNS Section 42(1)(a)]
- [BNS Section 111]
- [BNS Section 303]
- [BNS Section 314]

## Recommendation / next steps
Given the circumstances, an investigation into the alleged abduction/kidnapping of the minor should be conducted as per [BNS Section 20(1)(i)] to ensure the preservation of evidence and the protection of the minor's rights. The online interactions between the victim and the alleged perpetrator should be examined to gather more information. The authorities should also take necessary measures to locate and secure the safe return of the minor. 

As the alleged abduction/kidnapping is a serious offence, the punishment for this crime under [BNS Section 111] could be applied. The [BNS Section 314] could also be considered as a relevant section, considering the dishonest intentions of the alleged perpetrator.
