(c) makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any 
class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional 
group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause 
disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons; or 
(d) makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and 
integrity or security of India, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 

CHAPTER XII 
OF OFFENCES BY OR RELATING TO PUBLIC SERVANTS

[BNS Section 353] BNS_2023_s353 (Act: BNS_2023)
Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 
Exception.—It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person 
making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable 
grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence.—
(1) Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that 
he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time 
being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a 
term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand 
rupees. 
(2) If an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of false evidence referred to in 
sub-section (1), the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the 
punishment specified in sub-section (1).

Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description 
which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

omission shall take place in pursuance thereof.

(2) Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any case other than that referred to in

three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.

Explanation 2.—An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court, is a

## Summary
The employee in question has altered financial records in the company's accounting software to hide embezzlement. The question is whether this action constitutes the offence of 'dishonest misappropriation of property' under Clause 228 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and whether the employee should be prosecuted for this offence. Additionally, the question seeks investigative measures under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and the admissibility of digital evidence under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

- [BNS Section 1]

- [BNS Section 211]

1. **Prosecution under BNS for 'dishonest misappropriation of property'**: Given the employee's actions, it can be inferred that the employee has committed 'dishonest misappropriation of property' as per the illustration in [BNS Section 314]. The employee has been entrusted with the company's financial records and has dishonestly altered them for personal benefit, which constitutes a breach of trust.
2. **Investigative measures under Article 15 of BNSS**: The investigating authority may gather evidence through digital forensics, including examining the company's accounting software and any relevant data. The authority should also preserve digital evidence by seizing relevant devices and storage media.
3. **Admissibility of digital evidence under Section 35 of BSA**: The digital records and evidence obtained from the company's accounting software, including the altered financial records and any other relevant data, may be admissible in evidence as digital evidence under Section 35 of BSA. However, the conditions and requirements for admissibility, such as authentication and reliability, must be met to ensure the evidence is deemed admissible.

In conclusion, the employee's actions constitute the offence of 'dishonest misappropriation of property' under Clause 228 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). The investigating authority should gather evidence through digital forensics and preserve digital evidence. The digital records and evidence obtained may be admissible in evidence as digital evidence under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), subject to meeting the conditions and requirements for admissibility.

Pursuant to Section 123(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), wherein an "offence by a company" is defined, and Section 124(3) of the BNS, which prescribes liability for "conspiracy" by a group of individuals, I respectfully seek clarification on the following:

Is an organized gang operating a fake call center, impersonating tax officials, and extorting money from people under threat of arrest, liable to be proceeded against under the provisions of BNS Section 123(1) for being an "unlawful assembly" and BNS Section 124(3) for conspiracy, with further implications under BNSS Section 53(2) (b) for "offences against public justice" and BNS Section 130(1) (c) for "criminal breach of trust"?

Additionally, under the provisions of the BNSS, what constitutes sufficient evidence under BSA Section 59(2) (a) to establish the identity of the gang members, and can the testimony of victims under BSA Section 60(1) be considered as primary evidence in prosecuting this case?
result.answer:
## Summary
The organized gang operating a fake call center, impersonating tax officials, and extorting money from people under threat of arrest is liable to be proceeded against under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). They may be charged with organized crime under Section 111, conspiracy under Section 124(3), and criminal breach of trust under Section 314.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 111] Organised crime
- [BNS Section 124(3)] Liability for conspiracy by a group of individuals
- [BNS Section 314] Criminal breach of trust

## Recommendation / next steps
To establish the identity of the gang members, sufficient evidence under BNS Section 59(2)(a) would be required. The testimony of victims under BNS Section 60(1) can be considered as primary evidence in prosecuting this case. The organized gang may be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than five lakh rupees under Section 111.

## Summary

The political leader's speech is likely to have incited violence and promoted social enmity between Hindus and Muslims. The utterances made by the political leader may constitute an offence under Section 15(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Promoting Social Enmity) as they are likely to promote disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred between different religious groups. The speech may also constitute an offence under Section 13(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Incitement to Violence) if it is likely to cause fear or alarm to the public.

The evidence adduced in this case may be admissible under Section 16 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (Hearsay and Admissibility of Oral Statements) if it meets the requirements of admissibility. However, the burden of proof under Article 17 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (Presumption of Innocence) would be applicable to the accused in this case, and the prosecution would need to prove the accused's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found.

Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.—Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as

or with fine, or with both, or with community service, and where a declaration has been made under 
sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with 
imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration.—(1) Whoever, by words either 
spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic communication or 
otherwise,—

members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith 
and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and 
integrity of India; or

their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, be 
denied, or deprived of their rights as citizens of India; or 
(c) makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any 
class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional 
group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause 
disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons; or 
(d) makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and 
integrity or security of India, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

Committee have been considered by the Government and it has been decided to withdraw the Bill 
pending in Lok Sabha and introduce a new Bill incorporating therein those recommendations made by the 
Committee that have been accepted by the Government.

attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other 
matter; or

electronic communication or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote, on grounds of religion, 
race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, 
disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or 
regional groups or castes or communities; or

religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, and which disturbs or is likely 
to disturb the public tranquillity; or

in such activity shall use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be likely that 
the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, or participates 
in such activity intending to use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be 
likely that the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, 
against any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community and such activity for 
any reason whatsoever causes or is likely to cause fear or alarm or a feeling of insecurity amongst 
members of such religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

Requesting a formal investigation and subsequent prosecution under the following sections:

- BNS, Article 301(1)(a) - Act endangering life or personal safety of others by fire or explosive substance, read with BNS, Article 304(B) - Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, in relation to the deliberate setting of houses on fire.
- BNS, Article 319(1)(g) - Voluntarily causing grievous hurt, in relation to the physical assault and subsequent rape of the woman.
- BNSS, Article 125(1) - Power to investigate cognizable offences, and BNSS, Article 128(1) - Arrest without warrant in accordance with law, for the apprehension and detention of the perpetrators.
- BNSS, Article 213(2) - Protection of witnesses and victims, in relation to the safety and security of the woman and her family.
- BSA, Article 15(2) - Presumption as to abetment of offence, for determining the culpability of the individuals involved in the riot.
- BSA, Article 17(3) - Relevant and admissible evidence, for the collection and presentation of evidence in the case.

Requesting an expeditious investigation and prosecution to ensure justice for the victims and their families.
result.answer:
## Summary

A petition has been filed for prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) in relation to the communal riots where a mob set fire to several houses and a member of the mob raped a woman whose family was fleeing. The petitioner is requesting a formal investigation and subsequent prosecution under various sections of the BNS and BNSS.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 303] - Act endangering life or personal safety of others by fire or explosive substance, read with [BNS Section 304(B)] - Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
- [BNS Section 319(1)(g)] - Voluntarily causing grievous hurt, in relation to the physical assault and subsequent rape of the woman.
- [BNS Section 46] - Abetment of an offence, for determining the culpability of the individuals involved in the riot.
- [BNS Section 195] - Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc., for the actions of the mob against public servants.
 
## Recommendation / next steps

An expeditious investigation and prosecution are recommended to ensure justice for the victims and their families. The authorities should proceed with the investigation under the provisions of the BNS and BNSS, and take necessary measures to ensure the safety and security of the witnesses and victims, as per [BNS Section 213(2)].

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the activities of the organized gang operating a fake call center, impersonating officials and extorting money from citizens by threatening them with arrest, constitutes an offence under Article 123(1) of the BNS, specifically, "Punishment for Cheating and Dishonesty" and/or Article 143(2) of the BNS, "Punishment for Criminal Conspiracy", and whether the same can be investigated and prosecuted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically, Section 37(3) of the BNSS, "Power to Investigate Cognizable Offences", and Section 49(2) of the BNSS, "Procedure for Investigation of Cases"? 

Furthermore, whether the evidence collected in the course of the investigation can be admitted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically, Article 10(2) of the BSA, "Relevance of Facts", Article 15(1) of the BSA, "Proof of Identity of Parties", and Article 18(3) of the BSA, "Proof of Documents"?
result.answer:
## Summary
The activities of the organized gang operating a fake call center, impersonating officials and extorting money from citizens by threatening them with arrest, constitute a serious offense under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). The offense falls under the categories of cheating and dishonesty, criminal conspiracy, and organized crime.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 148]: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147.
- [BNS Section 111]: Punishment for organised crime.
- [BNS Section 314]: Punishment for criminal breach of trust.
- [BNS Section 229]: Punishment for false evidence.

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the analysis of the BNS provisions, the activities of the organized gang can be investigated and prosecuted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). The evidence collected in the course of the investigation can be admitted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA). The offense can be charged under the categories of cheating and dishonesty, criminal conspiracy, and organized crime. The prosecution can seek imprisonment for a term which may extend to life, and also liable to fine, under the relevant provisions of the BNS.

repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Sanhita, 2023.

Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita.

omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India.

of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

result.rephrased_query: Whether the act of demanding Rs 50,000 from a poor patient's family for performing an emergency surgery and refusing to treat without payment constitutes the offence of "Demanding or Accepting Illegal Gratification" under BNS, Article 125(1) and "Neglect of Public Duty" under BNS, Article 237(2)(b), in light of BNSS, Article 12(1)(a), which mandates free and timely medical aid to all citizens. Furthermore, whether this incident amounts to an "offence" under BNS, Article 3(1) and, if so, is it a "cognizable offence" in accordance with BNSS, Article 19(4)(b), thereby warranting immediate arrest and investigation under BNSS, Article 21(2)(c).
result.answer:
## Summary

A doctor at a government hospital demanded Rs 50,000 from a poor patient's family to perform an emergency surgery and refused to treat without payment. This act may be considered an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), specifically in relation to "Demanding or Accepting Illegal Gratification" under BNS, Article 170 and "Neglect of Public Duty" under BNS, Article 222.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 170] Bribery
- [BNS Section 125] Act endangering life or personal safety of others
- [BNS Section 222] Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance
- [BNS Section 200] Punishment for non-treatment of victim

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the circumstances, the doctor's actions may be considered a form of bribery under BNS, Article 170, as they demanded payment in exchange for medical treatment. This is a punishable offence under the BNS. Additionally, the doctor's refusal to treat the patient without payment may be considered an act of neglect of public duty, as they failed to provide timely medical aid to the patient, which is mandated by BNSS, Article 12(1)(a). The doctor's actions may also be considered a form of omission to assist a public servant, as they refused to provide medical treatment to a citizen in need.

The doctor's actions may be punishable under BNS, Article 222, with imprisonment and/or a fine. Furthermore, the doctor's refusal to treat the patient without payment may also be considered a form of non-treatment of a victim, which is punishable under BNS, Article 200, with imprisonment and/or a fine.

In light of the above, it is recommended that the doctor be investigated and charged with the relevant offences under the BNS.

What constitutes the offence of 'terrorism' under the BNS, specifically in relation to the planting of an explosive device in a public place, resulting in the deaths of five individuals and grievous injuries to numerous others, in contravention of Article 15 of the BNS?

This petition is verified and certified to be true to the best of the petitioner's knowledge by the undersigned.

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we respectfully submit the following incident report and request for investigation:

**Incident Description:**

On [date], a woman, identified as [wife's name], is alleged to have committed an offence under Article 302 of the BNS, where she mixed poison into her husband's food, thereby attempting to cause his death. However, due to timely medical intervention, he survived the ordeal. Furthermore, it has been discovered that she had taken out a large life insurance policy on her husband, a week prior to the incident, as per Article 123 of the BNS.

**Request for Investigation:**

We request that an investigation be conducted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to determine whether the wife's actions constituted a criminal offence, and if so, to identify the relevant sections of the BNS that have been contravened. We also request that the investigation gather evidence to establish the wife's motive and intent behind taking out the life insurance policy.

**Request for Evidence Collection:**

Pursuant to Article 50 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we request that all evidence related to the incident, including medical records, witness statements, and insurance policy documents, be collected, preserved, and examined to determine their relevance to the investigation.

**Request for Proceedings:**

We request that the investigation be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the BNSS, and that the proceedings be recorded and preserved as per Article 75 of the BSA.

**Conclusion:**

We respectfully submit that the investigation and prosecution of this case are necessary to uphold the principles of justice and ensure that the law is enforced in accordance with the provisions of the BNS, BNSS, and BSA.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy', we inquire about the potential applicability of this provision to the group of perpetrators, considering the concerted and premeditated nature of their actions.

Additionally, in light of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses', we seek guidance on the procedures to be followed in registering and investigating this incident, as well as the measures that can be taken to safeguard the Dalit family's rights and interests.

## Summary

In the given scenario, a group of men forcibly entered a Dalit family's home, beat them severely, destroyed their household items, and hurled casteist slurs at them. This incident appears to be motivated by casteism. The perpetrators' actions can be analyzed under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Chapter V, Section 2, 'Offences Against the Body'
- Chapter VIII, Section 5, 'Offences Against Modesty'
- Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy'
- Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses' (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023)
- Chapter VII, Section 7, 'Relevant and Admissible Evidence' (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023)

## Recommendation / next steps

The perpetrators can be charged under the provisions of Chapter V, Section 2, 'Offences Against the Body' for assault, and Chapter VIII, Section 5, 'Offences Against Modesty' for outraging the modesty of the Dalit family members. Considering the concerted and premeditated nature of their actions, they may also be charged under Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy'.

For the registration and investigation of this incident, the procedures to be followed can be found in Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses' of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. Measures to safeguard the Dalit family's rights and interests should be taken according to this provision.

A man wearing a police uniform set up a fake checkpoint and collected fines from truck drivers on a national highway. This raises several questions regarding the applicability of BNS provisions and the criminality of the person's actions.

To determine whether the man's actions constitute an offense under the BNS, we need to examine each relevant provision:

- [BNS Section 59]: The man's actions may be considered as facilitating the commission of an offense (extortion) which it is his duty as a public servant to prevent. Therefore, he may be liable under this provision.
- [BNS Section 303]: Theft requires dishonest intentions. Since the man is impersonating a public servant and collecting fines, it is likely that he is acting dishonestly. Therefore, he may be liable under this provision.

- [BNS Section 353]: This provision deals with statements conducing to public mischief. The man's actions may be considered as causing fear or alarm to the public. Therefore, he may be liable under this provision.
- [BNS Section 199]: This provision deals with public servants disobeying directions under law. The man's actions may be considered as disobeying the law, as he is impersonating a public servant and collecting fines without authority. Therefore, he may be liable under this provision.

In conclusion, the man's actions may be considered as an offense under several BNS provisions, including [BNS Section 59], [BNS Section 303], [BNS Section 314], [BNS Section 353], and [BNS Section 199]. Further investigation and evidence would be required to determine the exact nature and extent of his liability.

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 
Exception.—It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person 
making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable 
grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

Public servant disobeying direction under law.—Whoever, being a public servant,— 
(a) knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the 
attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other 
matter; or 
(b) knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating 
the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation; or 
(c) fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 173 of the 
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in relation to cognizable offence punishable under 
section 64, section 65, section 66, section 67, section 68, section 70, section 71, section 74, 
section 76, section 77, section 79, section 124, section 143 or section 144, 
shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but 
which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Alternatively, considering the government clerk's actions as an abuse of public trust, the query can be rephrased as:

Moreover, the query can also be framed as follows in relation to the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023):

Lastly, considering the admissibility of evidence, the query can be rephrased as follows under the BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023):

## Summary

The government clerk intentionally prepared a false caste certificate for someone in exchange for a bribe. We need to determine if this act constitutes an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and, if so, what are the subsequent legal consequences.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 229]
* [BNS Section 211]
* [BNS Section 314]

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the BNS provisions, it appears that the government clerk's actions may fall under the category of "giving false evidence" or "dishonestly disobeying the directions" in the context of public service. 

Section 229(1) of the BNS states that whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees.

Section 211 of the BNS states that whoever, being legally bound to give any notice or to furnish information on any subject to any public servant, as such, intentionally omits to give such notice or to furnish such information in the manner and at the time required by law, shall be punishable.

Section 314 of the BNS states that whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

Therefore, the government clerk's actions may constitute an offence under Section 229(1) for giving false evidence or under Section 211 for omitting to give notice or furnish information, or under Section 314 for committing criminal breach of trust.

It is recommended that the government clerk be investigated and charged under the relevant provisions of the BNS. The subsequent legal consequences would depend on the outcome of the trial and the sentence imposed by the court.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer

Pursuant to Article 124 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), an incident has been reported where an individual, unidentified at this time, allegedly committed an act of vandalism and desecration at a temple, specifically:

1. Willfully causing damage to property (idol) by applying black paint, thereby intentionally causing harm to the property, in contravention of Article 215 of BNS.
2. Writing offensive graffiti on the walls of the temple, thereby violating the sanctity of the place of worship and potentially inciting communal disharmony, in contravention of Article 217 of BNS.

Pursuant to Article 45 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested that an investigation be conducted to apprehend the perpetrator and gather evidence.

Pursuant to Article 82 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the admissibility of the evidence of the black paint and graffiti as proof of the perpetrator's actions is sought.
result.answer:
## Summary

The individual in question has allegedly committed two acts: (1) willfully causing damage to the temple idol by applying black paint, and (2) writing offensive graffiti on the walls of the temple. These acts contravene Article 215 and Article 217 of BNS, respectively.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* Section 294: Offence of writing or drawing or engrafting any obscene or hurtful matter on any wall, or elsewhere.
* Section 324: Mischief.
* Section 197: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration.

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the nature of the alleged acts, the investigation should focus on gathering evidence to prove the perpetrator's identity and intent. The admissibility of the evidence of the black paint and graffiti as proof of the perpetrator's actions should be determined under Article 82 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

Section 294 is relevant as it deals with the offence of writing or drawing or engrafting any obscene or hurtful matter on any wall, or elsewhere. Section 324 is also relevant as it deals with the act of mischief, which involves causing damage to property.

Section 197 is relevant as it deals with imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration. Although the graffiti may not necessarily be an imputation or assertion, the act of writing offensive graffiti on the walls of the temple could potentially cause disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities.

Upon completion of the investigation, the relevant provisions of BNS should be applied to determine the appropriate punishment for the perpetrator.

Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), is the alleged perpetrator liable for the offence of outraging the modesty of a religious community, as purportedly committed by publicly ridiculing and disparaging the religious practices of another community during their festival procession, thereby potentially attracting punishment under Section 8(1)(a) of the BNS?

Additionally, please provide guidance on the application of Section 24 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the purposes of arrest, and the admissibility of evidence under Article 47 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically considering Section 31(2) thereof, regarding the testimony of eyewitnesses who may have been influenced by the communal tensions arising from the incident.

## Summary
The alleged perpetrator loudly abused and mocked the religious practices of another community during their festival procession. Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the query is whether the alleged perpetrator is liable for the offence of outraging the modesty of a religious community and potentially attracting punishment under Section 8(1)(a) of the BNS.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- Section 197
- Section 353
- Section 147 (referenced in Section 148)
- Section 123 (referenced in the query, however context for this section is not provided)

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the provided BNS sections, the alleged perpetrator's actions may be considered as an offence under Section 197 (Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration) or Section 353 (Statements conducing to public mischief). Section 197 deals with imputations or assertions that may cause disharmony or feelings of enmity between different groups, which seems to apply to the scenario. Section 353 deals with statements that may cause fear or alarm to the public or induce a person to commit an offence against the State or public tranquillity. The perpetrator's actions may also be seen as a conspiracy to commit an offence under Section 148 (Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147).

For arrest, the provisions of Section 24 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) may be applicable, specifically considering the circumstances of the incident. As for the admissibility of evidence, Article 47 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) may come into play, particularly Section 31(2) regarding the testimony of eyewitnesses who may have been influenced by the communal tensions arising from the incident.

A group of boys trespassed into a graveyard at night, dug up a grave, and stole jewellery from the corpse. The question is whether their actions constitute an offence punishable under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and whether the perpetrators can be held liable.

Based on the BNS provisions, it appears that the group of boys' actions may constitute an offence under the following sections:

- [BNS Section 148] for conspiracy to commit offences, as the boys may have conspired to commit a crime.

## Summary

The factory owner brought migrant workers from Bihar with false promises and made them work without pay under locked conditions. This office seeks clarification on the applicability of Section 117(1) of BNS, relating to "Exploitation of Labour" and Article 10(3) of the BNS, which defines "Cruel and Inhuman Treatment". Additionally, guidance is sought on the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 3(1) of BNSS, in relation to the alleged contravention of Sections 23(2) and 24(1) of BNS, which deal with "False Promises" and "Confinement for Labour", respectively.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Section 117(1) relating to "Exploitation of Labour"
- Article 10(3) defining "Cruel and Inhuman Treatment"
- Section 23(2) dealing with "False Promises"
- Section 24(1) dealing with "Confinement for Labour"

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the information provided, it appears that the factory owner may have committed offenses under Sections 23(2) and 24(1) of BNS, which relate to "False Promises" and "Confinement for Labour", respectively. The migrant workers were brought with false promises and made to work under locked conditions, which is a clear contravention of these sections.

To take further action, a First Information Report (FIR) should be registered under Section 3(1) of BNSS. The police should then investigate the matter and gather evidence to prove the offenses committed by the factory owner.

In terms of evidence, statements made by the migrant workers may be admissible under Section 59(1) of BSA, provided they are protected under Article 26(2) of BSA, which deals with "Protection of Accused Persons". However, this would depend on the specific circumstances of the case and the admissibility of the evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

It is essential to note that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) is the primary legislation governing the offenses committed by the factory owner. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) are secondary legislations that provide additional provisions and guidelines for the investigation and prosecution of crimes.

[BNS Section 4] BNS_2023_s4 (Act: BNS_2023)
Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

[BNS Section 1] BNS_2023_s1 (Act: BNS_2023)
Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Query: 
Pursuant to Article 43, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the actions of the seven armed men constitute the offence of "Dacoity" under Article 174, Clause 2, and if so, what are the relevant provisions of Article 43, Clause 1 for the determination of their liability, considering that they employed force or threat to gain entry and committed a breach of peaceful possession of the jeweller's shop, as per Article 43, Clause 2.

Additionally, under Article 56, Clause 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, whether the police have the authority to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant, given the circumstances of the breach of the peace and commission of dacoity, in accordance with Article 56, Clause 5.

Lastly, under Article 81, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what is the burden of proof that the prosecutor must establish to secure a conviction against the accused, and whether the testimony of the watchman, as a witness, will suffice to establish the chain of events, in accordance with Article 81, Clause 2.

## Summary
The seven armed men broke into a jewellery shop at night, tied up the watchman, and looted all the gold and cash. This incident raises questions about the application of various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023). The first query concerns whether this constitutes the offence of "Dacoity" and the relevant provisions for determining liability. The second query pertains to the authority of the police to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant. The third query seeks to establish the burden of proof for securing a conviction against the accused.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 254]
- [BNS Section 148]

## Recommendation / next steps
To address the first query, under Article 43, Clause 1 of the BNS_2023, the actions of the seven armed men could be considered as "Dacoity" as per Article 174, Clause 2. The relevant provisions for determining their liability are those related to harbouring robbers or dacoits, as stipulated in [BNS Section 254]. This section imposes punishment on individuals who harbour or conceal robbers or dacoits, with the intention of facilitating their activities or screening them from punishment.

Regarding the second query, under Article 56, Clause 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the police have the authority to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant, given the circumstances of the breach of peace and commission of dacoity, in accordance with Article 56, Clause 5.

Lastly, under Article 81, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the burden of proof that the prosecutor must establish to secure a conviction against the accused is through the testimony of the watchman, as a witness, which will suffice to establish the chain of events, in accordance with Article 81, Clause 2.

Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a query is raised regarding the commission of a punishable offense under the BNS by a male individual who wilfully misrepresented himself to a female individual as being lawfully married to her, thereby inducing her to cohabit with him for a period of several months. 

In this regard, it is requested to determine whether the aforesaid actions of the male individual could be characterized as an instance of 'cheating' (as defined under Article 123 of BNS) and, if so, what specific provisions of BNS would be applicable in this scenario.
result.answer:
## Summary
The man's actions of wilfully misrepresenting himself to the woman as being lawfully married to her, thereby inducing her to cohabit with him for several months, could be characterized as an instance of 'cheating' under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 314], [BNS Section 4]

## Recommendation / next steps
The man's actions could be punishable under Section 314 of the BNS, which deals with 'cheating'. According to this section, whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

In this case, the man has intentionally deceived the woman into believing that they were lawfully married, and thereby dishonestly induced her to cohabit with him. This meets the criteria for cheating under Section 314 of the BNS.

Therefore, the man could be charged under Section 314 of the BNS, and if found guilty, could face imprisonment of up to three years, or a fine, or both.

**Case Query for Legal Guidance**

Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, we seek clarification on the following situation:

A married individual (hereinafter "the accused") entered into a second marriage with another woman (hereinafter "the second wife") without disclosing his prior marital status. The question arises under Article 349(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether this act constitutes a cognizable offense against the institution of marriage, under Chapter XIX, and whether the accused's failure to disclose his marital status constitutes a punishable offense, as per Section 117 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Furthermore, in light of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, we request guidance on the procedure to be followed in investigating this matter, specifically under Chapter X, Section 53(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Lastly, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, we seek clarity on the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly in relation to the second wife's knowledge or ignorance of the accused's prior marital status, as per Section 11(3) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

## Summary

A married individual entered into a second marriage with another woman without disclosing his prior marital status. This act raises questions about whether it constitutes a cognizable offense against the institution of marriage and whether the accused's failure to disclose his marital status is punishable. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS_2023) will be used to guide the analysis.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 82]
* [BNS Section 2]
* [BNS Section 113]
* [BNS Section 303]
* [BNS Section 253]

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the situation, the accused's act of marrying again without disclosing his prior marital status could be considered a punishable offense under the BNS_2023. Section 82 of the BNS_2023 specifically deals with marrying again during the lifetime of a husband or wife, and Section 2 of the BNS_2023 defines an offense as any act committed outside India which, if committed in India, would be punishable under the BNS_2023.

The accused's failure to disclose his marital status to the second wife could also be considered a punishable offense under the BNS_2023, particularly if the second wife was unaware of the prior marriage.

Investigating this matter would involve procedures outlined in Chapter X of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically under Section 53(1) of that Act.

Admissibility of evidence in this case would depend on the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, particularly Section 11(3) of that Act, which deals with the admissibility of evidence in relation to a person's knowledge or ignorance of certain facts.

Therefore, the next steps would be to determine whether the accused's act constitutes a punishable offense under the BNS_2023, investigate the matter, and determine the admissibility of evidence in relation to the second wife's knowledge or ignorance of the accused's prior marital status.

Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been 
ordered.—Whenever any person convicted of or charged with an offence, being in lawful custody for 
that offence, escapes from such custody, or whenever a public servant, in the exercise of the lawful 
powers of such public servant, orders a certain person to be apprehended for an offence, whoever, 
knowing of such escape or order for apprehension, harbours or conceals that person with the intention of 
preventing him from being apprehended, shall be punished in the manner following, namely:— 
(a) if the offence for which the person was in custody or is ordered to be apprehended is 
punishable with death, he shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which 
may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; 
(b) if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years, he shall 
be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with 
or without fine; 
(c) if the offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year and not to ten 
years, he shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term 
which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for such 
offence, or with fine, or with both. 
Explanation.—“Offence” in this section includes also any act or omission of which a person is 
alleged to have been guilty out of India, which, if he had been guilty of it in India, would have been 
punishable as an offence, and for which he is, under any law relating to extradition, or otherwise, liable to 
be apprehended or detained in custody in India, and every such act or omission shall, for the purposes of 
this section, be deemed to be punishable as if the accused person had been guilty of it in India. 
Exception.—The provisions of this section do not extend to the case in which the harbour or 
concealment is by the spouse of the person to be apprehended.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by 
insulting its religion or religious beliefs.—Whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of 
outraging the religious feelings of any class of citizens of India, by words, either spoken or written, or by 
signs or by visible representations or through electronic means or otherwise, insults or attempts to insult 
the religion or the religious beliefs of that class, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description 
for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or

(2) Whoever threatens to assault or attempts to obstruct any public servant or threatens or attempts to

endeavouring to disperse an unlawful assembly, or to suppress a riot or affray, shall be punished with 
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration.—(1) Whoever, by words either

members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith 
and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and

(b) asserts, counsels, advises, propagates or publishes that any class of persons shall, by reason of

(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any

(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the

(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section

(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit

(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information,

community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable 
grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, and which disturbs or is likely 
to disturb the public tranquillity; or

in such activity shall use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be likely that

in such activity intending to use or be trained to use criminal force or violence or knowing it to be 
likely that the participants in such activity will use or be trained to use criminal force or violence, 
against any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community and such activity for 
any reason whatsoever causes or is likely to cause fear or alarm or a feeling of insecurity amongst 
members of such religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.

Pursuant to Article 32, Sub-article 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the following matter:

Whether an individual who enters the dwelling of another person without their consent (Article 1, Sub-article 2 of BNS) and causes damage to the property by rearranging furniture (Article 23, Sub-article 4 of BNS) commits an offence under BNS, and if so, what would be the corresponding punishment (Article 23, Sub-article 6 of BNS).

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), in the event of a threatening note being left at the scene (Article 17, Sub-article 2 of BSA), what burden of proof would lie on the accused to prove that the threat was not made with the intention of causing harm or intimidation (Article 17, Sub-article 5 of BSA), and what would be the admissibility of such evidence in the context of this incident (Article 19, Sub-article 3 of BSA)?

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what would be the procedure for the complainant to lodge a complaint in this matter (Article 12, Sub-article 1 of BNSS), and what would be the requirements for the investigation and collection of evidence in such cases (Article 15, Sub-article 2 of BNSS)?
result.answer:
## Summary
The individual entered the dwelling of another person without their consent, rearranged furniture, and left a threatening note. This raises issues under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) regarding whether such actions constitute an offence and the corresponding punishment.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 1]
- [BNS Section 2]
- [BNS Section 46]
- [BNS Section 209]
- [BNS Section 324]
- [BNS Section 303]
- [BNS Section 113]
- [BNS Section 211]

## Recommendation / next steps
Given the facts, the individual's actions of entering the dwelling without consent, rearranging furniture (which may constitute mischief), and leaving a threatening note, could be considered as an offence under the BNS. 

The punishment for mischief under [BNS Section 324] depends on the extent of the damage caused. If the damage is to the amount of twenty thousand rupees and more but less than one lakh rupees, the punishment would be imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

However, if the intention behind the actions was to cause wrongful loss or damage, the punishment could be imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both, under [BNS Section 324].

Additionally, the individual's failure to provide notice or information to the public servant regarding the commission of an offence, or to prevent the commission of an offence, or for the apprehension of an offender, could attract punishment under [BNS Section 211].

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted that the following incident is being reported for consideration under the following sections:

Whether the act of the drunk man amounts to an 'Offence Relating to Public Nuisance' under Article 174 of BNS, and does it necessitate an investigation under Article 179 of BNS for causing disturbance in a public place, namely a railway station.

Whether the use of 'filthy language' constitutes an 'Offence Relating to Defamation' under Article 189 of BNS, and does it necessitate an investigation under Article 179 of BNS.

Whether the act of the drunk man urinating on the platform in front of passengers amounts to an 'Offence Relating to Public Decency' under Article 197 of BNS, and does it necessitate an investigation under Article 179 of BNS.

Whether any cognizance can be taken against the drunk man under Articles 191 and 192 of BNS, considering his intoxicated state?

Whether the passengers at the railway station are liable to be examined as witnesses under Article 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to establish the facts of the incident, and whether any other relevant evidence can be collected under Article 41 of BSA.

Whether an arrest can be made under Article 85 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the commission of the aforesaid offences, and what procedure is to be followed under Article 91 of BNSS for the detention and production of the accused before a Magistrate?
result.answer:
## Summary
The incident reported involves a drunk man creating a ruckus at a railway station, using filthy language, and urinating on the platform in front of passengers. The main questions raised are whether these actions constitute 'Offence Relating to Public Nuisance', 'Offence Relating to Defamation', 'Offence Relating to Public Decency', and whether any cognizance can be taken against the drunk man considering his intoxicated state.

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 292] - Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for.
[BNS Section 353] - Statements conducing to public mischief.
[BNS Section 229] - Punishment for false evidence.

## Recommendation / next steps
Considering the actions of the drunk man, it can be concluded that he has committed a public nuisance at the railway station. Pursuant to [BNS Section 292], he shall be punished with a fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

As the drunk man's actions involve the use of filthy language, which may be considered as statements conducing to public mischief, he can be held liable under [BNS Section 353]. However, it is essential to note that the person making, publishing, or circulating any such statement must not have reasonable grounds for believing that the statement is true and must not make it in good faith.

Since the drunk man urinated on the platform in front of passengers, which can be considered as an act of indecency, it may amount to an 'Offence Relating to Public Decency' under [BNS Section 197] (not provided in the context). However, without the context section, we cannot confirm this.

Regarding the question of whether any cognizance can be taken against the drunk man considering his intoxicated state, it is essential to note that [BNS Section 209] deals with non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. It does not provide any information on how to handle cases where the accused is under the influence.

For further investigation and proceedings, the Magistrate may consider making an arrest under [BNS Section 85] (not provided in the context) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, and follow the procedure for the detention and production of the accused as per [BNS Section 91] (not provided in the context).

As per [BNS Section 23] (not provided in the context) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the passengers at the railway station can be examined as witnesses to establish the facts of the incident, and other relevant evidence can be collected under [BNS Section 41] (not provided in the context).

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been

subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Furthermore, under the provisions of Article 155 (3) Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is sought to clarify the process of filing an FIR and the subsequent investigation that should be conducted by the police, particularly in light of the fact that the complainant was provoked in a public place. 

Lastly, in relation to the admissibility of evidence, the relevant provisions of Article 78 (1) Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) should be applied to determine the weight and admissibility of the evidence that may be presented in connection with the alleged incident, including the testimony of witnesses who may have observed the verbal abuse.

## Summary

The user has been verbally abused by a neighbour in a public setting, and they wish to know the applicable provisions and the next course of action. The incident occurred in a public place, and the neighbour intentionally insulted the user to provoke a fight. The user wants to file an FIR and seek investigation by the police.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* Section 500 (1) BNS
* Section 127 (2) BNS
* Section 353 BNS
* Section 197 BNS
* Section 211 BNS
* Section 199 BNS

## Recommendation / next steps

The user may file a complaint with the police, as they have been a victim of verbal abuse in a public place. The police may register an FIR under Section 211 BNS, as the neighbour failed to give notice or information to the authorities. The police investigation may also consider Section 199 BNS, as they are a public servant and are required to conduct the investigation in a fair and impartial manner.

The user may also consider filing a complaint under Section 197 BNS, as the neighbour's verbal abuse was intended to cause disharmony or enmity between different groups of people. The police may also consider registering a case under Section 353 BNS, as the neighbour's statement was likely to cause fear or alarm to the public.

Once the FIR is registered, the police may conduct an investigation, and the user may be called as a witness to testify against the neighbour. The user should cooperate with the investigation and provide any evidence or testimony required by the police.

In addition, the user may consider seeking legal advice from a lawyer to understand their rights and the legal options available to them. The lawyer may also be able to provide guidance on how to navigate the court process and represent their interests in court.

A complaint has been submitted to the police regarding an alleged contravention of Articles 321 to 323 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), punishable under Article 325 of the BNS. The police are requested to examine the evidence and apply the principles of proof as enshrined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically under Article 17, to establish the guilt of the perpetrators.

If found guilty, the perpetrators should be brought to justice and punished accordingly.

The complainant also seeks to initiate proceedings under Article 27 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to recover the pecuniary loss incurred due to the acceptance of said counterfeit currency notes. Furthermore, the complainant requests that the accused be proceeded against under Article 43 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for the alleged destruction, suppression, or fabrication of evidence (i.e., the counterfeit notes) in relation to the said transaction.

The complainant has filed a case against the accused for allegedly using counterfeit five-hundred rupee notes to settle a payment for goods sold. The complainant seeks legal intervention under Article 225 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for forgery, recovery of pecuniary loss under Article 27 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and to proceed against the accused under Article 43 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for destruction, suppression, or fabrication of evidence.

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 178]

## Recommendation / next steps

Based on the context, the complainant's case falls under counterfeiting currency notes, which is punishable under [BNS Section 178]. The accused should be proceeded against under this section for the offense of counterfeiting currency notes. As for the recovery of pecuniary loss, the complainant can initiate proceedings under Article 27 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

The user's ancestral property has been fraudulently claimed through the production of a forged court order at the registrar's office. The user seeks a declaration under Section 13 of the BNS, specifically in relation to Section 3(a)(iii) of the BNS, with a prayer for restitution of the ancestral property and a prayer for prosecution of the perpetrator.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* Section 1
* Section 3(a)(iii)
* Section 13
* Section 314
* Section 197

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the facts provided, the user may seek legal recourse by filing a petition under Section 13 of the BNS for a declaration and restitution of the ancestral property. The user may also seek prosecution of the perpetrator under Section 314 of the BNS for criminal breach of trust. Additionally, the user may consider filing a complaint under Section 197 of the BNS for making false or misleading information jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and integrity or security of India. The user should consult with a legal professional to determine the best course of action in this matter.

[BNS Section 1] BNS_2023_s1 (Act: BNS_2023)
Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

[BNS Section 4] BNS_2023_s4 (Act: BNS_2023)
Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.
